item.title: VCF 9.1.2 is out
item.description: What Broadcom shipped VCF 9.1.2 today. Most of it is aimed at getting AI and Kubernetes platforms up faster: An AI infrastructure quickstart: one vCenter plugin configures the cluster, turns on Supervisor and builds a VKS cluster. A VKS quickstart that gives you a working Supervisor and VKS cluster, plus a test environment with add-ons. Chained VKr upgrades. Pick the version you want and VCF works

item.title: New on vCloudOne: sizing calculators
item.description: What I've added three sizers to the site, one each for Amazon EVS, VMware Cloud on AWS and on-prem VCF. Drop in RVTools exports or type in workload totals and you get hosts, clusters and management overhead, with checks and an Excel export. EVS Sizing: hosts and clusters for Amazon EVS. VMC Sizing: SDDCs, clusters and hosts, with placement and DR per workload group, a topology diagram and a memory

item.title: Amazon EVS, one year in
item.description: Amazon EVS went GA a little over a year ago. Here's what changed since, what I think matters most, and what to look at if you're planning a move.

item.title: SDDC 1.26v5 is the new default build
item.description: What New SDDCs and upgrades now get SDDC 1.26v5. It's a security patch build with no new features. Who it's for Anyone keeping track of SDDC versions across an estate.

item.title: You can now raise the Elastic DRS storage warning
item.description: What The Elastic DRS storage warning used to be fixed at 65%. You can now move it up to 75% through the Autoscaler API. Why it matters If your SDDCs run storage-heavy, that 65% warning can go off during normal operation. Now you can set it closer to the point where you'd actually act. Because it's an API setting, it's easy to apply across several SDDCs. Who it's for Customers with storage-heavy SD

item.title: Amazon EVS gets r7i hosts, external principal storage and an Agent Skill
item.description: What Amazon EVS now supports r7i.metal-24xl and r7i.metal-48xl for VCF 9.x. These are memory-optimized hosts with no local NVMe, so AWS also added support for external principal storage. In practice that means Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP instead of vSAN. The EVS Deployment Orchestrator can create the FSx file system for you, and with FSx a simple deployment needs only 2 hosts. AWS also released an

item.title: vSphere Express, Live Recovery and DR built into VCF
item.description: What Broadcom announced a few changes to the VCF portfolio: vSphere Express , a new entry edition on vSphere 9 for up to 128 cores. It includes vMotion, HA, distributed switching and TPM security. Two new Advanced Services: VMware Live Recovery for disaster and cyber recovery, and VMware Compliance and Configuration Management . Disaster recovery built into VCF and VVF themselves, planned for the

item.title: Amazon EVS adds Osaka, Taipei, Spain and Tel Aviv
item.description: What Four more Regions: Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Europe (Spain) and Israel (Tel Aviv). Why it matters Add December's seven and July's three and that's fourteen new Regions in a year. More Regions help with data residency, and with DR designs that need a second Region close by. Who it's for Anyone who needs VMware workloads in Japan, Taiwan, Spain or Israel.

item.title: VCF 9.1.1 lands the week of VMware Explore
item.description: What VCF 9.1.1 came out the same week as VMware Explore in Las Vegas. The new features are mostly AI: Multi-Tenant Model Sharing lets several business units use one model deployment while keeping their data separate. AI Assistant for VCF is a chat assistant inside VCF Operations, and you choose the model provider. GitOps and native object storage showed up as tech previews. Both went GA in 9.1.2.

item.title: i7i.metal-48xl and the EVS Deployment Orchestrator
item.description: What Two things landed around EVS's first birthday. The i7i.metal-48xl is a bigger host on 5th Gen Intel Xeon, so you can run more VMs on fewer hosts. AWS says i7i gives up to 23% better compute and more than 10% better price performance than i4i. AWS also released the EVS Deployment Orchestrator (EDO) in the Solutions for Amazon EVS repo. You launch one CloudFormation stack and it builds the AWS

item.title: Three good reads: NSX Federation, DR and memory tiering on EVS
item.description: What AWS put out three design posts in one week: Aug 18: NSX Federation on EVS. One Global Manager spans on-prem and EVS sites, with shared segments and firewall policy. Aug 19: A walk-through of DR options for VMware workloads on EVS, from nothing pre-deployed to a full standby cluster. Aug 21: Using VCF 9 memory tiering to fit more VMs on each host. Why it matters These cover the questions that

item.title: SDDC 1.26v4 is the new default build
item.description: What Another security patch build. New SDDCs and upgrades now get 1.26v4. Nothing new to configure.

item.title: Amazon EVS arrives in Seoul, Zurich and Stockholm
item.description: What Amazon EVS is now in Asia Pacific (Seoul), Europe (Zurich) and Europe (Stockholm), with every existing feature, VCF 9.0 and 9.1 included. Who it's for Customers who need VMware workloads in Korea, Switzerland or Sweden.

item.title: Amazon EVS now runs VCF 9.0 and 9.1
item.description: What This is the big one for EVS this year. You can now run VCF 9.0 and 9.1 in every Region where EVS is available. EVS sets up the hosts and VPC networking, and you install VCF with Broadcom's VCF Installer. VCF evaluation mode is supported too, which is handy for proofs of concept. Why it matters VCF 9 brings memory tiering and the rest of the 9.x platform to AWS. Since the VCF install is now yo

item.title: SDDC 1.26v3: fixes and Secure Boot certificate updates
item.description: What A maintenance release with stability fixes. It also starts the platform work for Microsoft's expiring 2011 Secure Boot certificates. Who it's for Anyone running Windows VMs with Secure Boot on VMC.

item.title: You can now take EVS VCF issues straight to Broadcom
item.description: What Until now every EVS case went through AWS Support. If you have an active VCF subscription, you can now open VCF software cases directly with Broadcom. AWS Support still covers the whole stack, and Broadcom only covers the VCF software. Why it matters For a VCF software problem, going straight to Broadcom can save a hop. Anything about EC2 hosts, VPC networking or the EVS API still goes to AWS

item.title: Amazon EVS environments can now grow to 32 hosts
item.description: What The limit per environment went from 16 hosts to 32, through a service quota increase. You can run one big cluster or split the hosts across several. Why it matters Fewer, bigger environments mean fewer sets of management appliances to run and patch. It's a quota, so ask for it before you need it. Who it's for Anyone who has outgrown 16 hosts, or who runs several small environments that could

item.title: VCF 9.1 is here
item.description: What Broadcom announced VCF 9.1, the first feature release since 9.0, and it went GA later in May with an in-place upgrade from 9.0. The parts I'd look at first: Better memory tiering. You can turn it on without a reboot, and you can mirror the tier device in software. vSAN deduplication and compression on more cluster types. Live patching for ESX on TPM-enabled hosts, continuous compliance, and r

item.title: Amazon EVS adds the i7i.metal-24xl
item.description: What A smaller host than i4i on a newer CPU, aimed at better cost-performance for VMware workloads. Why it matters VCF is subscribed per core, so fewer, faster cores per host can save on licensing as well as on hosts. Who it's for EVS customers who want a smaller, newer host, or who are watching per-core costs.

item.title: Windows Server licenses on Amazon EVS
item.description: What You can now get Windows Server licenses from AWS for VMs on EVS, whether you migrate them or build them new. You add an entitlement per VM through an EVS vCenter connector, and billing is per vCPU-hour while the VM runs. Why it matters VMs without license portability rights used to need a separate licensing plan. Now you can cover them in EVS and remove the entitlement when you no longer need

item.title: Usage Report APIs for VMware Cloud on AWS
item.description: What Two new APIs: a Miscellaneous Usage Report for extra charges like Elastic IPs, Transit Gateway and data transfer, and a Microsoft SPLA Usage Report. They sit alongside the Host Usage Report API from last November. Why it matters You get daily usage data you can filter, so VMC spend can go into the same cost and BI tools as the rest of your cloud bill instead of waiting on invoices. Who it's f

item.title: HCX 4.11.4 for VMware Cloud on AWS
item.description: What A maintenance release of HCX. Like 4.11.3 before it, there's no WAN optimization appliance. Why it matters If any service mesh still has WAN-OPT appliances, you'll need to remove them before upgrading. Who it's for Customers migrating to VMC with HCX.

item.title: i7i.metal-24xl comes to VMware Cloud on AWS
item.description: What With SDDC 1.26v2, VMC supports i7i.metal-24xl for new and existing SDDCs in select Regions. It comes with host-to-host encryption, vSAN data-at-rest encryption and Intel TME memory encryption. A few things to know: existing SDDCs need to be on 1.26v2 first, vSAN ESA is only for new SDDCs or new secondary clusters, hyper-threading is on by default (96 logical cores per host), and stretched clu

item.title: Amazon EVS deployment prerequisites guide
item.description: What I wrote up everything EVS checks before it deploys VCF 5.x, in the order you'll need it: account and support plan, IAM, IP planning, VPC and subnets, Route 53, DHCP, VPC Route Server and BGP, capacity reservations, licensing and key pairs. It comes with a Terraform kit and a prerequisite validator. Why it matters EVS validates everything up front and fails fast if something is missing, so get

item.title: Multiple NSX Tier-0 gateways on Amazon EVS
item.description: What You can now run more than one Tier-0 gateway in an EVS environment, each on its own Edge cluster. Why it matters You can split north-south traffic for throughput, and keep environments like production and non-production (or different tenants) on separate routing and security policies. Who it's for EVS customers who need separate routing domains, more north-south throughput, or tenant isolatio

item.title: VCF 9.0.2 maintenance release
item.description: What A fix release for VCF 9.0. Two changes in vCenter 9.0.2 stood out to me: certificates issued by the VMware Certificate Authority for vCenter and ESX now renew automatically before they expire, and Supervisor control plane backup is on by default. Why it matters Expired certificates are a common cause of outages, so automatic renewal is a welcome change. If you're still on 9.0.0 or 9.0.1, this

item.title: Pick your VCF and ESX versions on Amazon EVS
item.description: What When you create an environment or add hosts, you can now choose a supported VCF and ESX version combination, from the console or the CreateEnvironment API. Why it matters It makes it easier to match the version you run on-prem during a migration, and to keep new hosts on the same build as the ones you already have. Who it's for EVS customers matching an on-prem VCF version, or expanding an ex

item.title: SDDC 1.26: vSAN ESA, bring your own key and VM hardware 21
item.description: What SDDC 1.26 moves VMC to vSphere 8.0 Update 3 and brings a lot with it: vSAN ESA is GA, with RAID-5 from 3 hosts. It's the default for new i4i deployments, for non-stretched SDDCs only. Bring your own key: VM encryption with an external KMIP key management system. VM hardware version 21, with up to 256 disks per VM and NVMe for Windows Server Failover Clustering. VMware Tools 12.5.4. Why it mat

item.title: Amazon EVS adds seven Regions
item.description: What Amazon EVS expanded to US West (N. California), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Milan), Mexico (Central) and South America (São Paulo). Who it's for Anyone who needs VMware workloads in those places.

item.title: VMware Cloud on AWS: December 2025 roundup
item.description: What Broadcom's December roundup covered a few changes: A redesigned console at vmc.broadcom.com. Stretched clusters can now scale down to 4 hosts (2 per AZ) or 2 hosts (1 per AZ), with some limits. HCX 4.11.3 drops WAN optimization and is supported until October 11, 2027.
